chunks: Ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Burayd al-'Ijli, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a Muslim man who put out the eye of a Christian, and he said: “Indeed, the compensation for the eye of a dhimmi is four hundred dirhams.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعُمِائَةُ: four hundred, the specified amount of compensation
key_terms.الذِّمِّيِّ: a non-Muslim under covenant protection in the Islamic polity
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: dirhams, the monetary unit of the compensation
key_terms.دِيَةَ: financial compensation due for bodily injury
key_terms.عَيْنِ: the eye, the injured organ under discussion
key_terms.مُسْلِمٍ: a Muslim man, the perpetrator mentioned in the legal case
key_terms.نَصْرَانِيٍّ: a Christian, identified here as the injured party

ai.seo_question: What is the diyyah for the eye of a dhimmi if a Muslim puts it out?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning bodily injury inflicted by a Muslim upon a non-Muslim under covenant protection. It specifies that the diyyah for the eye of a dhimmi is four hundred dirhams, indicating a fixed compensation in this case.
